South Central Kane County in southern Utah...

heavy rain across Buckskin Gulch, Wire Pass, and the Wave. Up to
0.75 inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

canyons, and normally dry washes.

Buckskin Gulch, Wire Pass, and the Wave.

This includes US Route 89 between mile markers 14 and 27.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River
drainage in combination with excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim near Bethel.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 715 AM AKDT, river gauges in Bethel have detected a rise in
water level above 8.5 feet. River gauge reports indicate rises in
water levels from the Kuskokwim River back-up in combination with
heavy rain across the advisory area. This is causing minor
flooding from overflow of poor drainage areas, especially along
the Kuskokwim.
- Strong onshore winds along the Kuskokwim coast have limited the
ability for the Kuskokwim River to drain out into the Bering Sea.
This has caused rapid river rises along the coast and inland into
Bethel. Water levels are expected to back up along Brown Slough
and flood low lying areas of Bethel and areas along the
Kuskokwim.
- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:
At 6:50am the stage was 8.6 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.
At 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown
Slough and flood low lying areas.
At 12.0 feet: Moderate flood stage.
At 14.0 feet: Major flood stage.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

If you live near or along the Kuskokwim River stay alert and be
prepared to take action.

properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Middle Yukon Valley, Lower Koyukuk Valley, Lower Yukon Valley, and
Innoko Valley.

Heavy rain is forecast to begin Monday afternoon. Rain should
continue through Wednesday morning with storm total rainfall of up to
2 inches expected. With already saturated ground conditions across
the region, the heavy rain may cause minor pooling/ponding of water
beginning on Tuesday.

Mainstem river flooding is not expected, but high water levels and
bankfull conditions are likely through the week as area rivers
respond to the rain. Localized flooding on smaller creeks and streams
is possible.

For more updated river information, please refer to water.noaa.gov or
weather.gov/aprfc.

properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* This (Monday) evening through Wednesday afternoon. Heaviest
rainfall expected late Tuesday morning through Tuesday night.

Rainfall:

* Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches Monday through Wednesday likely
won't be high enough for widespread flooding, but smaller
tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including Willow Creek and the
Little Susitna may reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.
